rationale: Round 3 plan: the round 2 overrides already met print_requirements.json; the deck changed in round 3 (screw holes at (+-36, +-25), six lead notches, switch hole), so it is sliced again. Stock 0.20mm QUALITY @MK3 + Prusament PETG (filament_type PETG = print_requirements; 250 °C, first layer 240, bed 90/85, fan 30-50 %: inside 230-250 / 80-90 and the skill's PETG range, so not overridden). Overrides meet print_requirements.json exactly as strength modelled the deck: 3 perimeters (1.26 mm), 5 top / 5 bottom layers (1.0 mm skins), 20 % gyroid, 0.2 mm layers. Not raised: strength passes on these, and the robot's mass budget (femur and knee servos) counts every gram. Elephant-foot 0.2 pairs with the 0.4 mm bed chamfer. Copies 1 = spec §7 (quantity 1, 5 h; sliced 2.74 h). Orientation is in the STL (brief): flat, underside on the bed, rails and PCA9685 posts standing up. No library rows (materials.csv and lessons.md are empty), so no flow, temperature or xy compensation overrides. Seam: aligned (stated explicitly), which keeps seams in corners and on round holes, off the ESP32 pocket's walls (0.6 mm clearance) and the post walls, where random would scatter them. Checked in the G-code: seams sit at the lead notch's corner (x 35, +y edge), the cable slots', ESP32 window's and pocket's corners, and on the round holes. The rear cable slots' corners at x -46 lie on the governing XY section (one-end lift, x -46.5, SF 3.54), where the bending stress runs along the loop, so staggered_inner_seams 1: the two inner perimeters now start 0.6-1.2 mm from the external seam (on the rear slots, on their long edge at x -45, where the stress crosses the loop) instead of lining up with it. That only moves where each inner loop starts: layers, Z and extrusion are unchanged (it is not a staggered-layer trick), and time went 2.73 -> 2.74 h. Brim: none (brim_width 0): 10,800 mm² of PETG bed contact, 8 mm tall, barely warps.
